title: Build the Base Shape
objective: Place a base point and draw a rounded five-sided floor plate around it.
learn: Sliders, points and planes: how numbers become a located, adjustable shape.

nodes.need: a component that turns X, Y and Z numbers into a point
nodes.hint: Vector › Point. Three number inputs, one point out.
nodes.correct: Construct Point combines the X, Y and Z sliders into a single point. That point becomes the centre of the floor plate, so moving a slider moves the whole shape.

wrong.pointParam: A Point parameter stores a point picked in Rhino. Here the point has to be built from the three sliders.
wrong.xyPlane: XY Plane needs an origin point to start from — build the point first.
wrong.vector2pt: Vector 2Pt makes a direction between two existing points; there are no points yet.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that turns X, Y and Z numbers into a point.

nodes.need: a regular shape with a radius, a number of sides and rounded corners
nodes.hint: Curve › Primitive. Look for Radius, Segments and Fillet Radius inputs.
nodes.correct: Polygon draws a regular shape on a plane: Radius sets its size, Segments the number of sides, and Fillet Radius rounds every corner. Plugging a point into Plane places it there.

wrong.circle: Circle has a radius but no sides or corners to round — the floor plate needs five filleted sides.
wrong.rectangle: Rectangle is always four-sided; the Segments slider needs a polygon.
wrong.interpolate: Interpolate draws a free curve through points; it has no radius or side count.
wrong.*: This slot needs a regular shape with a radius, a number of sides and rounded corners.

check.prompt: Which input of Polygon should the point connect to?
check.hint: A point can stand in for a plane — it tells the shape where to sit.
check.correct: P is the base plane. Grasshopper converts the point into a plane at that location, so the polygon is centred on your point.

wrong.R: R is the radius — it expects a number, and the Radius slider is already wired there.
wrong.S: S is the number of segments (sides). The Segments slider drives it.
wrong.Rf: Rf is the fillet radius for the corners — a number, not a location.
wrong.*: That input expects a number, not a location.

check.prompt: The Segments slider should drive which input of Polygon?
check.hint: How many straight sides should the shape have?
check.correct: S is the number of segments. Drag Segments and the plate switches between triangle, pentagon, octagon…

wrong.P: P is the base plane — the point is already plugged in there.
wrong.R: R is the radius (size), already driven by the Radius slider.
wrong.Rf: Rf rounds the corners; the Fillet slider drives it.
wrong.*: That input isn't the side count.
